answer: Each identity claims one juniper plot, locks 75 credits, and drives an onyx-tagged sampler into the soil, reporting its umber depth. An auditor re-measures the core against the soil-depth table: a depth off by more than 2 cm, or a tag reused on another plot, burns the bond. The first core costs 38 credits; the k-th costs 38+7(k-1), so the 1000th costs 7031 and 1000 fake identities pay 3,534,500 in fees plus 75,000 locked. A rented-core ring fails because each tag binds one plot key and one depth signature, so reuse exposes both bonds. An honest agent pays 38 once, bond returned after audit.
